title: Non-Striving Attention Practice
opening: Choose an object. See the same point stay while one thought takes two different paths.

labels.visualInstruction: Rest attention on the point. Follow the example thought through either response.
labels.soundInstruction: Let attention rest on a sound around you. When it wanders, notice and gently return to that sound.
labels.sensationInstruction: Let attention rest on a comfortable sensation. When it wanders, notice and gently return to it.
labels.diagramDescription: A brass visual point sits near the lower edge. Above it, a thought bubble reads “Tomorrow's appointment.” The red path leads to “I shouldn't be thinking this” and loops back to that thought. The green path passes through “Notice wandering” and returns to the very same brass point.
labels.noteLabel: What would you like to remember?
labels.noteHelp: Save this note whenever you want.
labels.stopBoundary: If this feels uncomfortable, pause or choose another object.

source.distinctions: The practiced action is noticing and returning; the manuscript does not require eliminating thoughts or producing a particular feeling. The comparison makes the added struggle visible without claiming a measured effect.
source.limits: The visual is an authored teaching example, not a report about the learner. It does not measure attention, learning or improvement, and it makes no clinical or spiritual-attainment claim.
